en.title: Building Your Alternate Infrastructure: The LatAm Tech-Business Bridge
en.excerpt: We build your second AI executive team in 6 months so you can focus on scaling your business.
en.content:
The Alternate Infrastructure Program

Our program is straightforward: we actively partner with the best companies for our program for a 6-month AI Lab journey. During the very first month, we deliver fully operational AI agents, immediately reducing your operational workload by at least 25%. From there, we build a personalized roadmap with periodic review and work sessions. By the end of the 6 months, you will have automated at least 70% of your operations, and more importantly, you will know exactly how to deploy, train, retrain, and integrate new agents without depending on anyone else. The AI Lab carries a fixed fee of $1,500 USD per month and includes the creation of custom AI agents, the setup of your orchestration platform, and our hands-on, highly personalized guidance.

We designed the WS AI Lab to be the first in Latin America capable of creating a complete alternate operational infrastructure in just 6 months. We literally build 'Second AI Directors,' Managers, and Assistants for every area of your business. The best way to explain this is through two of our recent partnerships:

The 40-Year Legal Legacy

A senior attorney came to us after working for 40 years the exact same way. He was managing over 200 active cases entirely alone. He wanted to rest, but he couldn't afford to hire a new team—training the right person, managing payroll, and overseeing errors was just too overwhelming. So, he joined our program.

In month one, we built an entire AI Legal Firm for him. We created a Managing Partner AI, specialized AI Attorneys across Commercial, Civil, and Administrative law, plus a drafting and expense assistant. We linked them securely to his Google Drive so they understand his files, collaborate with each other, and share deep memories of every client. We handed this to him ready to operate.

That's when the real work began. As he started using them, he ran into the friction of managing a 'new firm.' Through multiple hands-on sessions each month, we adjusted the architecture, refining the agents based on his direct feedback, and taught him how to program alongside us. By the end of the program, he has absolute control over his agents. He knows how to train them, scale them, and maintain them. We successfully gave him the tools to build his optimal team, and we moved on to our next client.

The Unbreakable Family Business

We partnered with a traditional, family-owned furniture retailer. They had many highly siloed departments: Finance handled by a brother, Administration run by the same person for 20 years without formal direction, a Production Engineer, a Logistics team of three coordinating delivery trucks, an external accountant, and Sales—the heart of the operation that needed to know everything.

During the first month, we built a 'second brain' for every department head. Each received a personalized assistant that responds to voice dictation to handle scheduling, internal communication, memos, and coordination. As the months continued, we analyzed their interactions during our work sessions and kept adding operational capabilities: generating financial reports, reconciling inventory, drafting contracts, handling work orders, and creating delivery receipts.

What we achieved together was a resilient organism. Today, if someone goes on vacation, a colleague just consults that person's AI assistant, who knows everything. If someone gets sick, anyone with a bit of company knowledge can step in, get up to speed instantly, and keep the work flowing. Everyone knows what they need to do. The agents execute the heavy operational lifting, leaving the vital, revenue-generating tasks to the humans. By the end of the program, no internal crisis can break them, because they built the perfect agentic communication tool alongside us in the AI Lab, and they know exactly how to train and command it.

es.title: Construyendo tu Infraestructura Alterna: El Puente Tecno-Comercial en LatAm
es.excerpt: Construimos tu segundo equipo directivo de IA en 6 meses para que tú te enfoques en escalar tu negocio.
es.content:
El Programa de Infraestructura Alterna

Nuestro programa es sencillo: solo aceptamos a las mejores compañías para nuestro programa durante un ciclo de 6 meses. El primer mes siempre entregamos agentes listos para trabajar, logrando que tu carga laboral baje al menos un 25% de inmediato, medido directamente con los agentes. A partir de ahí, trazamos un plan personalizado con sesiones periódicas de revisión y trabajo de la mano contigo. Al finalizar los seis meses, tendrás automatizado al menos el 70% de tus operaciones y sabrás montar tu propio sistema, entrenar, reentrenar y sumar nuevos agentes sin depender de nadie. El AI Lab tiene un fee fijo de $1,500 USD mensuales, e incluye la creación de agentes IA personalizados, el montaje de la plataforma de orquestación y nuestro seguimiento intensivo en tu plan de trabajo.

Hemos desarrollado nuestro AI Lab como el primero en Latinoamérica en crear tu infraestructura alterna completa en solo 6 meses, creando segundos Directores IA para cada área de tu empresa, Gerentes y Asistentes IA operativos. Para explicar mejor en qué consiste, lo contaré a través de dos ejemplos:

El Legado Legal de 40 Años

Llegó con nosotros un abogado que llevaba trabajando 40 años de la misma manera. Actualmente tenía más de 200 juicios que llevaba él solo; quería descansar pero no podía permitirse tener nueva gente por el desgaste de capacitar, encontrar a la persona adecuada o absorber la nómina. Decidió entrar al programa.

En el primer mes creamos para él una Firma Legal IA: un Socio Director IA, Abogados IA especializados en Derecho Mercantil, Civil y Administrativo, además de un asistente de redacción, agenda y gastos. Todos con acceso seguro a su propio Google Drive para que se entiendan, colaboren entre ellos y compartan memorias de cada cliente. Se lo entregamos listo para operar.

Ahí es donde realmente comienza la integración. Al operar, se topó con los problemas típicos de dirigir una 'firma nueva'. A través de múltiples reuniones al mes, realizamos ajustes basados en su plan de trabajo y le enseñamos a programar junto con nosotros. Al final del programa, él tiene control absoluto de sus agentes. Sabe cómo entrenarlos, mantenerlos y hacerlos crecer. Le dimos nuestras herramientas para que siga construyendo el equipo de lo que ya hace, de manera independiente, y nosotros continuamos con el siguiente cliente.

La Empresa Familiar Inquebrantable

Llegó con nosotros una empresa familiar dedicada a vender muebles, con muchos departamentos desconectados: finanzas a cargo de un hermano, administración llevada por la misma persona desde hace 20 años, un departamento de producción con un ingeniero, una logística con tres personas coordinando entregas, un contador externo y, finalmente, ventas, el corazón de la operación que necesita saber todo.

El primer mes les construimos un 'segundo cerebro' a cada cabeza de departamento: un asistente personal al que, por medio de dictarle con la voz, le delegan labores de agenda, envío de mensajes internos, memos y coordinación. Continuamos con ellos teniendo varias reuniones al mes. En cada revisión, analizábamos a sus asistentes y seguíamos sumando funcionalidades: hacer reportes, inventarios, escritos, contratos, arqueos, órdenes de trabajo y recibos de entrega.

Lo que logramos al final es un sistema donde, si alguien se va de vacaciones, solo se le pregunta a su asistente y él lo sabe todo. Si alguien se enferma, cualquier persona que conozca un poco la empresa puede tomar a su asistente, ponerse al día y tener todo el trabajo actualizado. Los agentes IA hacen el trabajo pesado, y el personal se concentra en las labores importantes de verdad; le dejamos las tareas que generan dinero a los humanos. Al final del programa, no los puede mover ninguna crisis, ya que saben cómo entrenar, crear y dirigir la herramienta de comunicación algorítmica perfecta para ellos, porque la desarrollamos juntos en el laboratorio.

en.title: Why Your Company Needs to Own Its Agent System
en.excerpt: The ROI of custom orchestration vs. closed SaaS platforms.
en.content:
The SaaS Trap

Relying on closed SaaS platforms for artificial intelligence usually results in fragmented workflows and data silos. While they offer quick onboarding, they inherently limit your ability to deeply integrate AI into your unique operational fabric.

The Value of Custom Orchestration

Investing in your own agentic orchestration platform is a paradigm shift. Although it requires an upfront commitment—such as our AI Lab Program ($1,500/month for 6 months)—the ROI is massive. You gain the ability to deploy bespoke agents that perfectly understand your specific context. More importantly, when you own the underlying architecture, your operational capacity scales infinitely without your software overhead scaling with it.

es.title: Por qué tu empresa necesita ser dueña de su sistema de agentes
es.excerpt: El ROI de la orquestación personalizada vs. plataformas SaaS cerradas.
es.content:
La Trampa del SaaS

Depender de plataformas SaaS cerradas para inteligencia artificial usualmente resulta en flujos de trabajo fragmentados y silos de datos. Aunque ofrecen un inicio rápido, limitan inherentemente tu capacidad para integrar profundamente la IA en tu tejido operativo único.

El Valor de la Orquestación Personalizada

Invertir en tu propia plataforma de orquestación agéntica es un cambio de paradigma. Aunque requiere un compromiso inicial—como nuestro Programa AI Lab ($1,500/mes por 6 meses)—el ROI es masivo. Ganas la capacidad de desplegar agentes a medida que entienden perfectamente tu contexto específico. Más importante aún, cuando eres dueño de la arquitectura subyacente, tu capacidad operativa escala infinitamente sin que tus costos de software escalen con ella.

en.title: The Breach: Why LatAm is the Next Frontier for AI Labs
en.excerpt: Analyzing the operational gap in Latin America and how high-fidelity AI agents can close it.
en.content:
The operational gap

Latin America has always suffered from a systemic infrastructure vacuum. While the global north optimization focus is on incremental gains, in LatAm, we are solving for zero-to-one infrastructure. Most businesses, even successful ones, spend 80% of their bandwidth on 'administrative noise'—legal hurdles, accounting complexity, and manual operations that have remained unchanged for decades.

The AI solution

WS Capital identifies this gap as the single largest opportunity for agentic deployment. By implementing networks that assume these roles with 99% precision, we allow the 20% of human talent—the genuine LatAm creativity and grit—to operate at 100% capacity. This isn't just about microchips; it's about freedom to execute.

es.content:
El vacío operativo

Latinoamérica siempre ha sufrido de un vacío infraestructural sistémico. Mientras que el norte global se enfoca en mejoras incrementales, en LatAm resolvemos por infraestructura de cero a uno. La mayoría de los negocios gastan el 80% de su capacidad en 'ruido administrativo'—trabas legales, complejidad contable y operaciones manuales que no han cambiado en décadas.

La solución IA

WS Capital identifica esta brecha como la oportunidad más grande para el despliegue agéntico. Al implementar redes que asumen estos roles con precisión del 99%, permitimos que el 20% del talento humano opere al 100% de su capacidad. No se trata solo de chips; se trata de la libertad para ejecutar.

en.title: Closing the Gap: Open Source AI as Digital Inclusion Infrastructure for Latin American SMEs
en.excerpt: The full research paper by WS Capital AI Lab. Empirical evidence on the digital divide, proposed solutions, and projected impact for 99.5% of Latin American businesses.
en.content:
Authors: WS Capital AI Lab
Date: May 2026
Version: 1.0

Executive Summary

Small and medium enterprises (SMEs) represent 99.5% of all businesses in Latin America and generate approximately 60-67% of formal employment in the region. However, their contribution to GDP is only 25%, revealing a structural productivity crisis rooted in the digital divide.

This paper presents empirical evidence that low technology adoption among Latin American SMEs is not a problem of willingness, but of access. Available business solutions suffer from prohibitive costs, extreme technical complexity, lack of integration with channels SMEs actually use (especially WhatsApp), and absence of continuous support.

We propose a new open digital infrastructure model based on three principles: (1) zero entry cost through free software, (2) conversational interface that eliminates the technical learning curve, and (3) native integration with tools SMEs already use. We present the case study of Hermes Business OS, an open source distribution that implements this model, and project its potential impact on productivity, employment and economic equity.

Central finding: If Latin American SMEs closed the digitization gap with large companies in the region, labor productivity could increase by up to 30%, with an estimated impact of 7.7% on regional GDP and the creation of more than 15 million jobs (IDB/World Bank, 2024).

1. Introduction

1.1 Context

Latin America is a region of entrepreneurs. According to ECLAC, there are approximately 12.9 million micro, small and medium enterprises across 17 countries. In Mexico, SMEs represent more than 99% of economic units and generate nearly 70% of formal employment.

However, average labor productivity in Latin America is only 33% of the OECD average in 2023; in 1990 it was 40%. The gap has widened, not narrowed. Micro-enterprises reach only 12.5% of the productivity of large companies in the region. In Europe, small businesses reach between 63% and 75% of large company productivity.

1.2 Hypothesis

The central hypothesis is that the productivity gap between SMEs and large companies in Latin America is primarily determined by the digital divide, and that this gap can be significantly closed through open, accessible technology infrastructure adapted to the Latin American context.

2. The SME Ecosystem in Latin America

2.1 Magnitude and composition

SMEs are the backbone of the Latin American economy: 99.5% of all businesses, 60-67% of formal employment, but only ~25% of GDP. 88.4% are micro-enterprises. This asymmetry is the symptom of a structural trap that ECLAC calls a low-growth capacity trap.

2.2 Productivity

Sectoral productivity relative to OECD: Commerce 33%, Manufacturing 39%, Other services 42%. Low SME integration reduces production chains, limits technology transfer, and slows productivity growth.

2.3 Digitalization potential

Digitalization can increase SME productivity by up to 30%. SMEs that invest in digital training increase productivity by up to 25% and reduce operating costs by more than 15%. Closing the connectivity gap with the OECD would create more than 15 million direct jobs with a 7.7% increase in regional GDP.

3. The Digital Divide

3.1 Infrastructure

67% of the Latin American population has internet access, below the global average. Only 2 in 5 households have internet access. More than 40% of households lack quality internet. The urban-rural gap is abysmal: Peru shows a 246.4% speed difference between urban and rural areas.

3.2 Digital skills

The deficit of trained digital professionals will reach 1.2 million by 2025. 68% of companies struggle to hire workers with desired skills. 55% of schools report lack of access or poor quality digital resources.

3.3 Technology adoption

96% of SMEs have no web presence. Only 23% have a functional website. Less than 10% use CRM or ERP. 75% of manufacturing companies use no form of digital monitoring. In Uruguay, only 10% of SMEs use data analysis systems; 40% still operate with physical paper records.

3.4 AI adoption

56% of SMEs are not generating tangible value with AI. Only 11% of companies in Latin America use AI. More than half of SMEs adopting AI operate in experimental stage. In Mexico, only 3% achieve advanced systemic AI integration.

4. Adoption Barriers

4.1 Economic

21% cite cost as the main barrier. Enterprise solutions require $5,000-$25,000 USD implementation. Hidden costs multiply total cost of ownership. Currency instability affects dollar-priced solutions. Credit access is limited: 22% rejection rate, only 25.3% access formal financing.

4.2 Complexity

Salesforce requires dedicated administrators. Zoho needs 2-4 weeks of configuration. Bitrix24 overwhelms with features. 73% of companies struggle to incorporate new technologies.

4.3 Integration

70% of SMEs sell through WhatsApp, yet no ERP or CRM was built for that flow. Systems are fragmented across 3-5 apps that don't communicate. Local tax regulations are not covered by global solutions.

4.4 Human factor

70% of digital transformation initiatives fail due to lack of organizational change. Technology alone is not enough without training and continuous consulting support.

5. Existing Solutions Landscape

5.1 Global solutions

Salesforce ($25-175/user/month), HubSpot (free to $100+), Zoho One ($37-90), Bitrix24 (free to $249). Verdict: powerful but expensive, complex, in English, no local tax compliance.

5.2 Local solutions

Alegra ($0-$1,999 MXN/month), Bind ERP ($570-$1,700 MXN/month), Siigo (~$20 USD/month). Verdict: cover invoicing and accounting but have limited CRM ecosystems and no native WhatsApp integration.

5.3 AI specific solutions

Fragmented across 4-6 different subscriptions to cover basic needs. Chatbots ($0-89/month), no-code automation ($20-50/month), generative AI ($13-20/month).

6. A New Model: Open Infrastructure for Digital Inclusion

6.1 Three principles

Principle 1: Zero entry cost through free software. SMEs cannot assume technology investment risks.
Principle 2: Conversational interface that eliminates the technical learning curve. 68% of companies cite lack of knowledge as their main barrier.
Principle 3: Native integration with tools they already use: Google Workspace, WhatsApp, Telegram.

7. Case Study: Hermes Business OS

7.1 What it is

Hermes Business OS (HBOS) is a distribution of native skills for Hermes Agent (Nous Research's conversational AI framework) designed specifically for Latin American SMEs. It transforms the AI agent into the company's operational partner.

7.2 Included skills

6 modules: Business Core (configuration, routing, Google Workspace), Sales (CRM, quotes, pipeline), Operations (projects, tasks, checklists), Documents (PDFs, contracts, proposals), Finance (budgets, payments, reports), HR (teams, attendance, payroll). Zero licensing cost.

7.3 Technical architecture

Agent Core: Hermes Agent (Python, open source). Dashboard: Next.js 15 + React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind. Document Engine: Python + WeasyPrint. Data: Google Sheets + JSON local. Communication: Telegram (primary) + Dashboard (secondary). 72 automated tests. Installation: under 5 minutes.

8. Projected Impact

Direct: 60-80% reduction in repetitive administrative tasks. Over 90% of documents generated without human intervention. Response time reduced from hours to minutes.

Sectoral: Up to 30% SME productivity increase. Over 15% operating cost reduction.

Macroeconomic: If 50% of SMEs reached basic digital maturity: +7.7% regional GDP, +15 million direct jobs.

Adoption scenarios: Conservative (10% digitalized, +0.8% GDP, 5 years), Moderate (25%, +1.9%), Ambitious (50%, +3.9%), Transformation (80%, +6.2%).

9. Conclusions and Recommendations

Conclusions: (1) The digital divide is the main bottleneck for SME productivity. (2) Existing solutions were not designed for Latin American SMEs. (3) The open infrastructure model with conversational interface solves economic, technical and integration barriers simultaneously. (4) Technology alone is not enough: accompaniment, training and cultural change are equally important. (5) The potential impact is massive.

Recommendations for policymakers: Adopt free software standards in SME digitization programs. Fund accompaniment, not just technology. Promote conversational digital literacy. Integrate fintechs with open infrastructure. Create industry-specific adoption clusters.

Recommendations for tech ecosystem: Design for the 99.5%, not the 0.5%. Prioritize WhatsApp over web apps. Embrace open source as a distribution model. Invest in conversational agents in Spanish.

Read the full paper with complete references at the GitHub repository. Explore the open source project: Hermes Business OS on GitHub.

es.title: Cerrando la Brecha: IA Abierta como Infraestructura de Inclusión Digital para las PYMES Latinoamericanas
es.excerpt: El paper de investigación completo del WS Capital AI Lab. Evidencia empírica sobre la brecha digital, soluciones propuestas e impacto proyectado para el 99.5% de los negocios latinoamericanos.
es.content:
Autores: WS Capital AI Lab
Fecha: Mayo 2026
Versión: 1.0

Resumen Ejecutivo

Las PYMES representan el 99.5% del tejido empresarial de América Latina y generan aproximadamente el 60-67% del empleo formal en la región. Sin embargo, su contribución al PIB es de apenas el 25%, revelando una crisis de productividad estructural con raíces en la brecha digital.

Este documento presenta evidencia empírica de que la baja adopción tecnológica entre las PYMES latinoamericanas no es un problema de voluntad, sino de acceso. Las soluciones disponibles sufren de costos prohibitivos, complejidad técnica extrema, falta de integración con los canales que usan las PYMES (especialmente WhatsApp), y ausencia de acompañamiento continuo.

Proponemos un nuevo modelo de infraestructura digital abierta basado en tres principios: (1) cero costo de entrada mediante software libre, (2) interfaz conversacional que elimina la curva de aprendizaje técnico, y (3) integración nativa con las herramientas que las PYMES ya usan. Presentamos el caso de estudio de Hermes Business OS y proyectamos su impacto potencial.

Hallazgo central: Si las PYMES latinoamericanas cerraran la brecha de digitalización, la productividad laboral podría aumentar hasta un 30%, con un impacto estimado de 7.7% en el PIB regional y la creación de más de 15 millones de empleos.

1. Introducción

1.1 Contexto

América Latina es una región de emprendedores. Existen aproximadamente 12.9 millones de micro, pequeñas y medianas empresas. En México, las PYMES representan más del 99% de las unidades económicas y generan cerca del 70% del empleo formal. Sin embargo, la productividad laboral promedio es solo el 33% del promedio de la OCDE.

1.2 Hipótesis

La hipótesis central es que la brecha de productividad entre PYMES y grandes empresas está determinada por la brecha digital, y que esta puede cerrarse mediante infraestructura abierta y culturalmente adaptada.

2. El Ecosistema PYMES

99.5% de las empresas, 60-67% del empleo, pero solo 25% del PIB. Las PYMES están atrapadas en una trampa de baja capacidad para crecer. La digitalización puede aumentar su productividad hasta en un 30%.

3. La Brecha Digital

67% de la población tiene acceso a internet, solo 2 de cada 5 hogares tienen acceso. 96% de las PYMES no tiene presencia web. 56% de las PYMES no genera valor tangible con IA. Solo el 11% de las empresas usa IA.

4. Barreras de Adopción

Económicas: costos prohibitivos, implementación costosa, financiamiento limitado. Técnicas: soluciones diseñadas para empresas con departamentos de TI. Integración: 70% de las PYMES vende por WhatsApp pero ningún sistema fue diseñado para ese flujo. Factor humano: 70% de las transformaciones digitales fracasan por falta de acompañamiento.

5. Soluciones Existentes

Las globales son potentes pero caras, complejas y en inglés. Las locales cubren facturación pero tienen ecosistemas limitados. Las de IA están fragmentadas. Una PYME necesita 4-6 suscripciones para cubrir lo básico.

6. Modelo Propuesto

Tres principios: cero costo de entrada (software libre), interfaz conversacional (sin curva de aprendizaje), integración nativa (WhatsApp + Google Workspace).

7. Caso de Estudio: Hermes Business OS

Distribución de skills nativos para Hermes Agent. 6 módulos: núcleo, ventas, operaciones, documentos, finanzas, RRHH. Cero costo de licencias. 72 tests automatizados. Instalación en menos de 5 minutos.

8. Impacto Proyectado

60-80% de reducción en tareas administrativas. Hasta 30% de aumento en productividad PYMES. Si el 50% de las PYMES alcanzara madurez digital: +7.7% PIB regional, +15 millones de empleos.

9. Conclusiones

La brecha digital es el principal cuello de botella. Las soluciones existentes no fueron diseñadas para PYMES latinoamericanas. El modelo de infraestructura abierta resuelve las barreras simultáneamente. La tecnología sola no basta: el acompañamiento es clave.

Lee el paper completo con referencias en el repositorio de GitHub. Explora el proyecto open source: Hermes Business OS en GitHub.

en.title: Democratizing Elite Data Architectures
en.excerpt: Bringing McKinsey-level strategic research to the independent entrepreneur.
en.content:
Information Asymmetry

Historically, high-level strategic data was gate-kept by massive consulting firms and prohibitive price tags. This creates an unfair advantage for incumbents. WS Capital is building a gateway based on open-source intelligence architectures and Andrej Karpathy's LLM research to break this wall.

The Open Protocol

Our goal is simple: an entrepreneur in a garage in Medellin should have the same research power as a VP in Manhattan. We are mapping global industry patterns into a queryable, high-fidelity knowledge graph accessible to all our partners.

es.title: Democratizando la Arquitectura de Datos de Élite
es.excerpt: Llevando la investigación estratégica nivel McKinsey al emprendedor independiente.
es.content:
Asimetría de Información

Históricamente, los datos estratégicos de alto nivel estaban bloqueados por grandes consultoras y precios prohibitivos. WS Capital está construyendo un portal basado en arquitecturas de inteligencia open-source e investigación de Karpathy para romper este muro.

El Protocolo Abierto

Nuestro objetivo es simple: un emprendedor en Medellín debería tener el mismo poder de investigación que un VP en Manhattan. Estamos mapeando patrones industriales globales en un grafo de conocimiento de alta fidelidad accesible para todos nuestros socios.
